trajectory_summary: This is a warm, self-generated lead (Tesla owner wanting solar to charge it) that the rep handled efficiently through verify and into a booked appointment. The call's shape is mostly flat-to-positive: no real objections, minor date-shuffling near the end, but the rep left clear value on the table by not flipping the captured bill number or deepening the Tesla-driven interest into a stronger hook.

observed_outcome.quote: So 12PM noon on, Friday, the seventh.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Friday the 7th) and time (12PM noon) are locked in for a specialist to 'stop by,' indicating an in-person appointment; the wife/co-owner was identified as a title holder but never explicitly confirmed for attendance.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured a strong bill figure but immediately pivoted to a logistics question about average kWh ('And let's see. 4,000 is kind of average throughout the year') rather than reflecting the dollar amount back as a reason to act; the flip should have landed right at 02:26.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep never raised getting the physical/digital utility bill (text, email, photo, login) at any point in the call — bill amount was captured verbally but the underlying document was not requested, likely deferred to the closer's visit.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: I just got a Tesla. And as I was thinking about it, I was like, hey. What if I just charge this off of the sun?
interest_reason_audit.use_quote: Well yeah. And then I'll make a note here, that you got a Tesla. So are you planning on charging from home then?
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep does circle back to the Tesla/EV detail at 03:13, but only to log a logistics fact for the design team rather than reinforcing it as the customer's stated motivation or using it to build urgency toward the appointment — a partial, non-persuasive callback rather than a full use of the interest reason.

script_coverage.quote: Hey, Kyle. This is Joel with ION. Just saw you were looking into some details on solar for your home and things and everything.
script_coverage.customer_quote: Good. How are you? Good. I'm doing good. Thanks for asking.

script_coverage.quote: But what kinda had you interested in solar?
script_coverage.customer_quote: I just got a Tesla. And as I was thinking about it, I was like, hey. What if I just charge this off of the sun?

script_coverage.quote: So first, I have your address here as the 8975 Kugler Mill Road in Cincinnati. Is that correct?
Is there anyone else on the title of the home with you at all?
script_coverage.customer_quote: Yeah. My wife. It's actually in her name, I think, officially.

script_coverage.quote: Are you what company are you going through for your electricity?
And how much is kind of an average electric bill costing you with them?
The only requirement is that either of you guys has a credit score of 650 or higher. Would that be the case there for you?
script_coverage.customer_quote: I haven't checked in a long time, but probably shouldn't have an issue there.

script_coverage.quote: So 12PM noon on, Friday, the seventh.
I'll get that on my calendar here, and I'll send you a text with the day and time.

objections.quote: No. Actually, I've got something tomorrow.
attempt_quotes: Would tomorrow around 12PM noon work good for you, or is there a better time?
Yeah. We could go for Monday the third. Is that day working for you?
How about Friday the seventh? Does that work?
objections.reasoning: Customer declined tomorrow, then the week-of-third Monday, then Wednesday, before landing on Friday the 7th at noon; the rep stayed flexible across each pivot until a date stuck.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: bill anchor captured but never flipped
primary_coaching_focus.why: This is the single clearest, most consequential gap on an otherwise smooth call — a big, specific bill number was handed over and the rep moved straight into the next verify item instead of using it to strengthen the customer's own case for showing up to the appointment.

key_moments.quote: I just got a Tesla. And as I was thinking about it, I was like, hey. What if I just charge this off of the sun?
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer just bought an EV and self-generated the solar idea from wanting to charge it — this is a higher-load, highly qualified enthusiasm signal, plus a natural bridge to mention Ion carries the Tesla Powerwall for backup.

key_moments.quote: We've got, you know, a van. I mean, it's, like, six or 7,000 square feet. So... I think we use about 4,000 kilowatt hours a month.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer hands over a large usage figure unprompted alongside home size context — a strong anchor — and the rep files it ('trying to get a feel for what something might look like') without reflecting it back as a hook.
A high, specific bill figure is captured cleanly, but the rep's very next line moves straight to averaging kWh rather than using the number emotionally.

key_moments.quote: Okay. Gotcha. Sounds good. And let's see. 4,000 is kind of average throughout the year per kilowatts per month?
key_moments.stewart_read: Immediately after hearing a $500-600 bill, the rep pivots to a logistics question instead of flipping the bill into emotional leverage against the utility.
